The first experiment gave very similar NLL values across all models (~-20.9), indicating this single condition is not discriminative. Most models fit similarly well, suggesting the baseline curve is well-described by simple MM behavior. This is expected - I need to design experiments that stress different mechanistic features.

M7, M16, M17 are marginally best but the differences are tiny. I need experiments that expose deactivation, dimerization, product inhibition, and activation phenomena.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
To discriminate, I should vary catalyst concentration significantly. This tests:
- Dimerization (M2, M3, M13, M19): rate has non-linear dependence on [cat]
- Catalyst activation (M6, M8): induction period more visible at low [cat]
- Deactivation (M9, M13, M14, M18, M20): more incomplete conversion at low [cat]/[S] ratio
- Simple MM (M1): linear rate with [cat]

A low-catalyst experiment with high substrate loading extends the reaction time so deactivation can manifest as plateau. Also increases catalyst-related sub-reactions (dimer formation more likely with more time).

Contrastive predictions for [S]=2.0, [cat]=0.002, [P]=0:
- M1: Slow but complete conversion, standard MM.
- M2, M3 (dimer eq): M3 has active dimer - very slow at low [cat]. M2 sequesters cat as inactive dimer, less pronounced at low [cat].
- M6, M8 (activation): Clear induction period at low [cat].
- M9, M11, M13, M14, M18, M19, M20 (deactivation): Plateau far below full conversion since deactivation timescale becomes comparable/faster than turnover.
- M12, M17 (product inhibition): Deceleration as product builds; final conversion slow but full.
- M4 (different catalyst species X): rate limited by X, not [cat].
- M7, M16 (second substrate binding): Substrate inhibition; slow initial rate.

Different plateau/final conversion behavior will discriminate deactivation vs product inhibition vs completion.
</hypothesis>
